newsitem.title: MACAU: Portugal's Sampaio opens China JV.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's Sampaio opens China JV.

text.p: Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio on Wednesday opened a Sino-Portuguese $23 million transformer-producing joint venture in China's northeastern Liaoning province, said a spokesman for the project in Macau.
"Today is a historic moment of concrete cooperation between businessmen from our two countries," Sampaio said, adding that he expected more Sino-Portuguese joint ventures in future.
The factory, Liaoyang EFACEC Electric Equipment Company in Liaoyang city, employs about 400 workers earning an average 650 yuan (US$78.3) per month and will start production in April.

Two-thirds of the joint venture is owned by mainland Chinese parties while the balance is held by the Macau-incorporated EFACEC-Oriente Limitada, owned by EFACEC Empresa Fabril de Maquinas Electricas, S.A.
Sampaio is travelling with a 180-strong delegation, including 40 businessmen from Portugal and Macau.
The delegation is scheduled to visit Pudong in Shanghai on Saturday before returning to Lisbon on Sunday.
